headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, primarily data centers, to bear the costs of new electric generating and transmission capacity, preventing these costs from being passed on to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Governor Abigail Spanberger, State Senator Louise Lucas, residential ratepayers, environmental advocates.
opponents: Data Center Coalition (concerned about language, but committed to paying full costs).
news_headline: Virginia Bill Shifts Grid Costs to Data Centers
news_summary: A new Virginia law aims to reduce residential energy costs by requiring data centers and other large energy users to pay for the increased electric generating and transmission capacity they demand. This shift is projected to significantly increase costs for data centers while decreasing rates for residential customers.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water suppliers report the water consumption of data centers to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency and enabling better water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental advocates.
opponents: Data center industry (initially questioned being singled out, but generally compliant with reporting).
news_headline: Virginia Law Mandates Public Data Center Water Reporting
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to publicly report the water usage of data centers. This aims to provide greater transparency and better inform decisions regarding water resources, especially as data center water consumption is a growing concern.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for large data centers, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Virginia League of Conservation Voters, community advocates, residents concerned about noise and siting.
opponents: Not explicitly stated in available information.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Mandates Data Center Siting, Noise Assessments
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153, now law, requires a permit process for high-energy data centers, mandating site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools. Localities can also require assessments of potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources, increasing transparency in data center development.
